findings.title: Required-case mapping still says eight EOF/death scenarios; the repaired test and README body say ten
findings.body: The repaired `pf_27_s01_admission_real_peer_eof_death_receipt_drop_and_caller_drop` now iterates `for scenario in 0..10` (five per role, adding the buffered-EOF `e`/`x` cases), and README line 31 states "Ten actual journal/policy EOF/death/receipt/caller scenarios". The `## Required-case mapping` table (not labeled retained history) still describes the same test as "eight actual journal/policy cases" and omits the buffered-marker variants that constitute the Astra30 repair evidence. Since this table is the durable requirement-to-observation map for the closeout record, the stale count misdescribes what the repaired admission log proves. Smallest fix: update the row to ten cases and mention the buffered (unread marker) EOF/death variants for both roles.

overall_explanation: Read-only inspection of the runtime diff over 6d770938c found no landable-blocking defect. Admission runs only on the existing pair supervisor thread with non-blocking calls (try_recv, SO_PEERCRED/SO_PEERPIDFD getsockopt, zero-timeout poll, MSG_PEEK|MSG_DONTWAIT, try_clone). UID is compared against a non-root expected UID that must equal the launching process UID; role derives solely from `OwnedChild::is_same_process` pidfs identity (false once reaped), and duplicate/parent/unrelated/dead peers are rejected without fencing the pair because `take_result` takes the control before returning a consumed rejection. Ticket drop, receipt drop, receiver loss, cancellation/deadline, child exit, and the repaired POLLRDHUP+peek monitor all set sticky cancellation and shut down the retained clones, so blocked readers wake even with unread bytes buffered (the kernel repro and the before/after regression logs support this). Drop order (stop → children → control → admission) and the spawn-failure path preserve Stage A permit/cleanup rules; a full or disconnected queue returns the caller's stream. Evidence checks: HEAD's `codex-rs` tree hash equals the recorded `5a4ee88b…`, total changed lines are 892 as claimed, all 17 `repair-tmux/*.exit` files (including `bazel-parity.exit`) plus `repair-suite.exit` are tracked and zero, and per-log summaries match the README counts. The only issue is a stale count in the required-case mapping table, recorded as a P3 documentation finding. No tests or mutating commands were run.
